C-V1. A Charts view is a data source that applies an aggregation pipeline to a collection to pre-process its data before Charts uses it. You can create more than one view from the same collection. C-V2. Only a Project Owner can create, modify, or permanently delete a Charts view. C-V3. A view pipeline must be an array of stage objects. C-V4. The documented uses are joining collections with `$lookup`, hiding sensitive fields with `$project`, and converting types (the documented example uses `$addFields` with `$toDate`). C-V5. Data source pipelines with `$lookup` arrived in v1.6.0 (2019-09-03).

C1. A Charts view is a data source that applies an aggregation pipeline to a collection to pre-process data before it is used for Charts. One collection can have several views. C2. Only a Project Owner can create, modify or delete a view. C3. A view pipeline must be an array, with each stage an object in the array. C4. The documented uses are joining collections with $lookup, hiding fields with $project, and converting data types; the docs example for type conversion uses $addFields with $toDate. C5. Aggregation pipelines on data sources, including $lookup joins, arrived in Atlas Charts v1.6.0

In scope: the pipeline that Atlas Charts generates to render a chart (the "backing aggregation pipeline"), the user-supplied pipeline entry points that feed it (query bar, charts views, embedding filters, pre-filters), stage support and restrictions, and the dated history of these features.

15. A charts view is a data source that applies an aggregation pipeline to a collection before Charts uses it. One collection can have several charts views. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/create-manage-charts-view/ 16. Only a user with the `Project Owner` role can create or change a charts view. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/create-manage-charts-view/ 17. A charts view can use `$lookup` to join collections, hide sensitive fields, and convert data types. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/charts/create-manage-charts-view/

**Out of scope:** chart types, dashboard layout, embedding authentication, the Charts REST API, cost, and the general MongoDB aggregation framework. General framework limits appear only where they bound a chart query.

Out of scope: Charts in general, chart types, dashboards as a product, the Embedding SDK beyond its pipeline-injection behaviour, Atlas Search, and the general MongoDB aggregation framework. Those are separate frontier items.

Charts does not support `$lookup` in query-bar aggregation queries, though it works in data source pipelines.
